(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The employee’s allergen certificate expired in June of 2026. Discussed getting re-certified to ensure that the certificate is valid. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: A wiping cloth intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces was observed hanging from the side of the sani bucket. Discussed with PIC and the cloth was placed inside of the sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths intended for sanitizing are always stored inside of the solution and never hanging from the sides of the bucket.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The house made spicy mayonnaise stored in the walk in cooler is incorrectly date marked. The date marking exceeds the temperature/time combination requirement. PIC mentioned that the spicy mayonnaise was made yesterday, April 16, 2025 and discard date for the sticker was April 30, 2025. The date sticker was corrected to April 23, 2025. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. Any sauce made in house can be held up to 7 days after the date that it is prepared. Day 1 counts as day of preparation and Day 7 is the very last day that the sauce can be kept in house. Discard at the end of the day if sauce exceeds the 7 day timeframe.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a container of chipotle mayonnaise to not be date marked in the walk in cooler. Overall, date marking was great for items in the prep cooler, however, same thing applies for items in the walk in cooler. Any TCS food items that are made in house will need to be date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation. The chipotle mayonnaise was date marked by the PIC. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) PIC was not following the requirements of the company HACCP plan and did not have a copy of any necessary documentation to discuss the requirements in detail. Missing documentation included, but was not necessarily limited to, the company HACCP plan, letters of guarantee for sushi fish, and employee health documents. Daily log book showed information written down for pH of sushi rice and calibration of pH meter and thermometer, but information was documented without the processes actually occurring based on the information provided. PIC has been working at the facility for ~2 months and stated they’ve never calibrated the pH meter or used it to verify pH of acidified rice. PIC was also not calibrating or using the available digital probe food thermometer and initially didn’t know they had a thermometer until they were advised as to which tool was the thermometer by inspector. PIC did not have proof of a food manager certification and stated they did not have any type of certificate when asked about training. In addition, priority violations were observed for handwashing and cross contamination. PIC also did not appear to understand the process of wash, rinse, and sanitize when asked to clean and sanitize a rice scoop removed from container of sushi rice. PIC was also unfamiliar with the requirements of proper cooling. Active managerial controls were discussed as best they could be at time of inspection, and inspector briefly spoke with regional manager during inspection (see general comments for additional information). Follow-up inspection will be conducted early next month to revisit active managerial controls and verify operations are conducted in accordance with the company HACCP plan and that all necessary documentation is available for the facility.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 PIC did not have proof of food manager certification. Per phone conversation with regional manager, PIC should have a manager certification, but PIC indicated they did not have a certification and did not know what inspector was referencing when asked for certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (C)(2), (3) and (17) Employee health documents were not available due to the absence of the company HACCP plan at the facility. Ensure employee health policy and all required documents are available and maintained at the facility. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Ensure a cleanup/disinfection policy is available and maintained at the facility. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided for reference. 
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC handled cell phone and did not wash their hands before putting on gloves to handle food. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and PIC washed their hands at request of inspector. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed upon entering the prep area, before putting on gloves to handle food, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Damp wiping cloth was placed on top of rice cooker after removing from the prep table. Sanitizer solution was not available for storage. PIC stated the handwashing sink was used to wet the wiping cloth prior to wiping the table. Proper use of handwashing sink for handwashing only was discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Do not use the handwashing sink for any purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
findings.citation_text:
3-402.12 Letters of guarantee were not available for sushi fish. Ensure proper documentation is available and maintained at the facility for all raw sushi fish served in ready to eat form.
If raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked fish served or sold in ready to eat form are frozen by a supplier, a written agreement or statement shall be provided from the supplier stipulating that the fish supplied are frozen to a temperature and for a time specified under § 3-402.11. If raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked fish are served or sold in ready to eat form, and the fish are raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4), a written agreement or statement from the supplier or aquaculturist stipulating that the fish were raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4) shall be obtained by the PIC and retained in the records of the food establishment for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale of the fish.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Rice scoop was stored in a tub of cooling rice in the walk-in cooler. Handle of scoop was in direct contact with rice. Handles of in-use utensils are not considered clean surfaces and should never be stored in direct contact with ready to eat foods. Scoop was removed and proper storage was discussed. 
2) Tempura shrimp out for sushi prep were sitting in contact with a damp paper towel, wiping cloth, and soiled surface behind prep surface. Shrimp in question were discarded.
3) Wiping cloth was observed in direct contact with sliced cucumber in a container out for use in the prep area. PIC noted wiping cloth was used to absorb excess moisture. Use of disposable paper towels was discussed for this practice. Cucumber in contact with wiping cloth was discarded. 
4) Foods in reach-in cooler were observed sitting on the shelf wrapped in paper towels that were soaked through. One item observed was raw fish, and other paper towel wrapped foods were said to be personal foods. Proper storage of products in food grade containers was discussed as well as storage of personal foods in a separate designated area. Raw fish was placed in a container.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw fish products, including thawing tuna, were observed on the top shelf in the reach-in cooler above and next to ready to eat foods. Proper storage of raw food was discussed, and PIC was advised to move raw fish to bottom of cooler below and separate from ready to eat foods. Raw food storage will be revisited at follow-up inspection after PIC receives additional training.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Ready to eat, TCS foods in reach-in cooler were observed without date marks, including but not necessarily limited to spicy crab salad, shrimp, tempura shrimp, and spicy mayo prepared on-site. Date marking was discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 White rice in the walk-in cooler cooked prior to inspector’s arrival was observed with surface temperatures of 79F-102F and internal temperatures of 111F-124F. Rice was said to be mixed with rice vinegar and sugar prior to placing it in the cooler ~30 minutes prior. Rice pH was not verified and cooling process was not being monitored. Plastic container was tightly sealed with a lid on top. Lid was left partially askew to allow for faster chilling of product, and PIC was advised on quick chilling of cooked rice. Company HACCP policy requires proper cooling of sushi rice if it will not be used immediately. Cooling will be discussed during training and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portion of vacuum packaged tuna was observed on the top shelf in the reach-in cooler. Instructions on package state to remove fish from package and thaw under refrigeration. PIC was advised to cut the package upon removal from freezer prior to placing in cooler to allow for proper thawing. Ensure packaging is cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the cooler. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in  (B) of this section.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloths were out in prep area. Two wiping cloths were taken to soiled linen storage, and the third wiping cloth was placed in sanitizer solution for storage. Store wet wiping cloths properly in sanitizer solution between uses or in soiled linen storage when no longer needed.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) PIC was not following the requirements of the company HACCP plan. Freshly prepared sushi products were not properly chilled to 41F prior to placement in the display cooler. Internal temperatures of several products were observed well above 41F. The coldest internal temperatures were observed at 42F and 42.5F for Quinoa salmon rolls and California spring rolls prepared during morning hours of operation. Sushi prepared in the afternoon had internal temperatures at 49.5F and 54.5F for crunch California rolls and 74.1F for shrimp tempura roll just prepared upon arrival of inspector. Proper chilling of sushi after preparation was discussed. 
Daily log book was also missing documentation. Temperatures of products, pH of sushi rice and other information is to be documented in the daily log book per the company HACCP plan. The last date of documentation was observed on 1/15/23. PIC was advised information is to be documented throughout daily operations to ensure accuracy and compliance with the HACCP plan.
Follow-up inspection will be conducted later this month to revisit active managerial controls and verify operations are conducted in accordance with the company HACCP plan.
 Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Surface temperature of brown rice was observed at 46F-49F and internal temperature was 52.3F. Rice was in a covered plastic container in the walk-in cooler. PIC indicated the rice was made around 8am and placed in the cooler around 9am to begin cooling process. PIC also indicted the rice should be cooled by the time it was checked by inspector around 2:30pm. Temperature was not monitored during cooling process. Based on information provided, the rice had another 30 minutes to reach 41F/below. Rice was placed in the walk-in freezer to finish rapid chilling.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink stored on top shelf of the prep table. Employee drinks must be stored below food or food contact surfaces or in a designated area to avoid contamination in the event of a spill. The drink was moved during the inspection. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the prep table without being held in sanitizer. Ensure wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer in between uses. 
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed no sani bucket available during the inspection. Ensure sani buckets are prepared and available for use during all hours of food preparation. A sani bucket was prepared during the inspection. 
(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed the quat sani bucket concentration to be 0ppm. Ensure the concentration of quat is maintained between 200ppm and 400ppm. The sani bucket was replaced during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Observed no sani bucket upon arrival during the inspection. The PIC prepared a sani bucket during the inspection. Also, wiping cloths were not placed in sanitizer solution. Ensure a sani bucket is available and made with wiping cloths inside it during all hours of operation. This is to keep all equipment surfaces clean and sanitized at all times. 
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed no sanitizer buckets or sanitizer spray available and being used to clean food contact surfaces during the inspection. A sanitizer bucket must be used and maintain a quat concentration of 200ppm-400ppm. A sanitizer bucket was made during the inspection.
